validity_findings: Synthetic tautology / construct validity threat: The derived_context for alias-OOD tasks is constructed by binding the expected_template (which contains the novel alias form) then parsing it back via derive_state. The reconstruction's choose_adoptions function then 'adopts' observed keys not present in registry candidates — since the test template's alias keys are directly observable in headers_observed/body_observed/url_query (by construction), this is a copy mechanism, not semantic resolution from real browser state. Producer acknowledges this in validity_notes #2, #8, #11 and report.md 'synthetic easiness'.

Zero live BrowserGym tasks: PC-BROWSERGYM-HEALTH FAIL (browsergym/playwright ModuleNotFoundError). Per frozen spec decision_rule, live stratum is exploratory and claim bounds to synthetic pooled only — correctly NOT MEASUREMENT_INVALID. Director mandate explicitly required live-browser WebShop/ALFWorld at BrowserGym 0.14.3 1280x720 with real CDP AX trees — untested.

Zero learned GRPO/System-One metrics: RECONSTRUCTION-LEARNED unavailable (transformers/torch ModuleNotFoundError). Core Director question asked for learned adapter matching rule proxy within 0.10 correct / 0.05 ECE with 3-seed training cost/stability reporting — completely untested.

Calibration evidence fragile: ECE 0.0803 computed over 5 bins with 3 empty bins (bins 1-3 count=0). Confidence distribution bimodal (~0.058 for 18 abstain-proximal, ~0.912 for 52 executable) driven by 0.80 gate + deterministic jitter, not emergent calibration. Bootstrap CI [0.0722, 0.0883] reflects this artifact. Producer acknowledges in validity_notes #3.

Intent equality confound: All 40 alias-OOD tasks use identical intent string between test query and registry mechanisms. B-EXACT-MATCH fails because template differs, not because intent differs. This isolates template aliasing but does not test retrieval where intent strings differ. Producer acknowledges in validity_notes #5.
B-RAG-EMBED unavailable: sentence-transformers ModuleNotFoundError. TFIDF used as strong retrieval baseline per frozen spec. Large-corpus embedding retrieval stress untested.

Mixed multi-channel composition test (10/10 correct) uses generic alphabetically-sorted adoption of observed keys not in registry. Tests composition of single-channel rewrites but within synthetic tautology (test template's multi-channel keys directly observable). No live mixed-channel test.

No end-to-end economics measured: Training cost/stability for LEARNED (wall-clock, tokens/calls, CV across seeds 42,43,44) untested. RULE economics trivial deterministic linear scoring. Verification-boundary economics (retrieval+reconstruction+verification cost per successful task vs RAG vs verbatim) not measured beyond trivial scoring.
baseline_findings: B-EXACT-MATCH: 0/40 correct on alias-OOD pooled (kernel L97 exact intent equality, min_confidence 0.8). Correctly fails because test intent equals registry intent but template aliasing requires reconstruction.

B-VERBATIM-REPLAY: 0/40 correct, 40/40 false_accept = 1.0. Retrieves first intent-matching mechanism and replays stored template verbatim. Measures maximal negative-transfer harm on alias-OOD. McNemar vs RECONSTRUCTION-RULE false_accept: b=0, c=40, p=6.98e-10.

B-RAG-TFIDF: 0/40 correct. TF-IDF retriever over intent+template strings, fit on train registry only. Fails because intent held equal and template strings differ. Does not test retrieval where intent differs.
B-RAG-EMBED: Unavailable (sentence-transformers ModuleNotFoundError). Per frozen spec, TFIDF serves as strong baseline for S5 domination gate.
B-RANDOM: 0/40 correct. Uniform random among intent-matching mechanisms. Chance-level baseline.

RECONSTRUCTION-RULE (genuine rule-based): 40/40 correct, 0 false_accept, 0 UNKNOWN. Structural scorer+rewriter with multi-channel adoption (choose_adoptions + rewrite_template_multi). Softmax temp 0.15 + deterministic jitter, gated UNKNOWN<0.80. Confidence std=0.3746.
RECONSTRUCTION-LEARNED: Unavailable. No GRPO/System-One training executed.

claim_ceiling: RECONSTRUCTION-RULE (genuine rule-based structural scorer+rewriter with multi-channel adoption via choose_adoptions + rewrite_template_multi) achieves perfect alias resolution on synthetic controlled tasks: 30/30 orthogonal header/body/auth families (including 9/9 held-out novel forms) + 10/10 mixed multi-channel (header+body+query within one request), with 0 false accepts, calibrated abstention (ECE 0.0803, 5 bins), and not dominated by retrieval baselines. Bounded to: minimal derived dict (url/method/url_path/url_query/url_segments/headers_observed/body_observed; no AX tree), intent strings held equal across registry/test, synthetic tautology (derived_context constructed from expected_template), bimodal confidence from 0.80 gate, no live BrowserGym WebShop/ALFWorld at 1280x720, no learned GRPO/System-One adapter, no production-SPA heterogeneity, no large-corpus retrieval stress. Does NOT establish learned non-inferiority, live-browser generalization, calibration beyond bimodal artifact, or cross-site parameterized transfer.
